abstract:
Climbing the tower adds fermionic modes; descent is the way back down, from the enlarged algebra to what an observer can see. [[t]] For a single mode it keeps the occupation data and erases the quantum coherence between empty and occupied. [[c:singularity.descent-what-it-erases]]

That erasure is the same as averaging over fermion parity. [[c:singularity.descent-parity-average]] Whatever the starting state, what survives can be read as a thermal state at one temperature. [[c:singularity.descended-form-state-independent]]

For an entangled horizon pair, under a geometric premise fixing the period, the temperature is the Hawking temperature. [[c:singularity.modular-descent]] The walk ends by asking what it costs to keep what the descent throws away, and finds that parity sets the price. [[c:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode]]
introduction: The walk first says what descent is, then shows how it makes states look thermal, and finally weighs the cost of undoing it. [[t]] Each result appears after the ones it rests on. [[t]]
i:descent: This section follows a single fermionic mode down from the enlarged algebra and then asks what the journey lost. [[t]]
t:^>singularity.descent-what-it-erases:
Everything here concerns one fermionic mode, a slot that is either empty or occupied, built from a null pair $v$, $v^*$. [[c:singularity.descent-what-it-erases]] With the projector $P = v^* v$, the descent keeps the diagonal of a two by two block and discards the rest: \[ E\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & d \end{pmatrix} \] [[c:singularity.descent-what-it-erases]]

The entries $a$ and $d$ are the occupation data; $b$ and $c$ are the coherences that make the mode a quantum superposition. [[c:singularity.descent-what-it-erases]] This is the basic operation the rest of the walk studies. [[t]]
t:singularity.descent-what-it-erases>sin:
The erasure has a cleaner description in terms of symmetry. [[t]] Averaging an observable with its parity-flipped version gives exactly the descent: \[ E(x) = \tfrac12\bigl(x + \sigma x \sigma\bigr) \] [[c:singularity.descent-parity-average]]

So $E$ is the unique conditional expectation onto the parity-even observables, it kills the odd sector, and every parity-even state passes through it unchanged. [[c:singularity.descent-parity-average]]
t:singularity.descent-parity-average>sin:
Once coherences are gone, a mode is left with just two probabilities. [[t]] Any such pair can be written as a thermal (Gibbs) state, \[ E_k(\varrho_k) = \frac{e^{-\beta_k \omega_k N_k}}{Z_k} \] for a unique inverse temperature $\beta_k$, whatever state the mode started in, provided its weight $\omega_k$ is not zero. [[c:singularity.descended-form-state-independent]]

So the thermal form after descent comes for free; the open question is which temperature. [[c:singularity.descended-form-state-independent]]
t:singularity.descended-form-state-indep:
To fix the temperature one needs a clock, and the mode supplies its own. [[t]] Its null pair combines into a single element \[ \sigma = v^* v - v v^* , \qquad \sigma^2 = 1 , \] which in the hyperbolic atom is the unit boost bivector $e_0 e_1$ of the plane. [[c:singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair]]

The rotor flow of $\sigma$ scales $v$ and $v^*$ by opposite weights, as a boost does to outgoing and ingoing horizon modes, and its spectral projectors are exactly the occupation projectors the descent uses. [[c:singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair]] So the clock is not a choice. [[t]]
t:singularity.modular-structure-complete:
A mode at a horizon comes with a partner on the other side, and the joint state of the two matters. [[t]] If that joint state is unchanged by the boost, apart from a phase, and genuinely entangled, it must have the form \[ \Omega = \cos\theta\,|00\rangle + \sin\theta\,|11\rangle \] with both coefficients nonzero. [[c:singularity.schmidt-forcing-proved-outright]]

The entanglement pairs empty with empty and occupied with occupied, and only the balance $\theta$ between the two terms is left free. [[c:singularity.schmidt-forcing-proved-outright]]
t:singularity.schmidt-forcing-proved-out:
With the shape of the pair's state fixed, descent to one side can be computed. [[t]] A pure, boost-invariant, entangled pair state descends to a state that is KMS (thermal) for the flow $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{it\sigma/2})$ at some inverse temperature $\beta$, but these conditions alone leave $\beta$ free, its sign included. [[c:singularity.modular-descent]]

Adding the geometric normalisation (R), which ties the state's intrinsic time to the horizon's period, gives exactly the Hawking temperature with Fermi-Dirac occupation. [[c:singularity.modular-descent]] The conditions are sufficient, not necessary. [[c:singularity.modular-descent]]
t:singularity.modular-descent>descent-li:
The walk now turns from what descent produces to what it destroys. [[t]] Written with the parity monomials $\G^{\kappa}$ of the modes, the descent on the even sector of $
u$ modes is \[ \EN(ho) = 2^{1-
u}\sum_{\kappa_{
u} = 0}\G^{\kappa}ho\,\G^{\kappa} \] half the flips it needs in general. [[c:descent-lift.kraus-form-descent-even-states]]

On a single mode it changes nothing. [[c:descent-lift.kraus-form-descent-even-states]] For a pair it sends $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ to $\operatorname{diag}(c^{2}, s^{2})$, erasing precisely the coherence that makes the pair entangled. [[c:descent-lift.kraus-form-descent-even-states]]
t:descent-lift.kraus-form-descent-even-s:
If descent erases entanglement, one can ask what it would cost to keep it in an extra record instead, a so-called lift. [[t]] An even lift needs $2^{
u-1}$ orthonormal even record states, and the even sector of $k$ rungs has dimension $2^{k-1}$, so for $
u \geq 2$ the record needs $k \geq 
u$ rungs: one rung of the tower per mode. [[c:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode]]

Such a lift exists with $
u$ rungs, on a record prepared in a paired state. [[c:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode]] Preparing that state from an empty record, though, needs dynamics that changes particle number. [[c:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode]]
t:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-m:
The count of one rung per mode looks generous for a pair, so the next result asks where the extra rung comes from. [[t]] For an entangled pair, two one-rung recipes exist as maps: Stinespring's minimal dilation and the occupation copy. [[c:descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-rung]]

Both are odd, so neither is an operation the univalence rule allows, and nothing else stands in the way. [[c:descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-rung]] Parity alone forces the second rung. [[c:descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-second-rung]]
t:descent-lift.parity-alone-forces-secon:
A worked example shows the lift in action. [[t]] For the series' sample pair, with $(c, s) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35)$, the two-rung lift is the pure, even four-mode state \[ c\,\ket{00} \otimes (\ket{00} + \ket{11}) + s\,\ket{11} \otimes (\ket{00} - \ket{11}) \] up to normalisation. [[c:descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduced-view-pure]]

The pair's marginal is $\operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{16}{25}, \tfrac{9}{25})$, exactly the classical shared bit the descent leaves. [[c:descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduced-view-pure]] The entanglement has not gone: it now sits between pair and record, with the same Schmidt coefficients. [[c:descent-lift.classical-shared-bit-reduced-view-pure]]
conclusion:
Descent is parity averaging, it makes every mode look thermal, and for a pure, boost-invariant, entangled horizon pair the temperature is Hawking's once premise (R) fixes the period. [[c:singularity.modular-descent]]

For two or more modes, undoing it costs one rung per mode, a price set by the univalence rule that physical states have even fermion parity. [[c:descent-lift.lift-costs-one-rung-per-mode]] Those two conditions, univalence and the geometric normalisation, are the ones this trail leans on, and both appear as stated conditions in the results rather than as separate assumptions. [[t]]
